questions.question: Describe how education policy has changed since 1944 and evaluate the impact of these changes.

points.text: 1944: tripartite system (grammar, secondary modern, technical) - reproduced class inequality. 1965: comprehensives - reduced stigma but streaming reproduced inequality. 1988: marketisation (league tables, Ofsted, choice) - benefits middle-class parents. 2010+: academies and free schools - mixed evidence on impact. Overall: policies have not significantly reduced class inequality.

questions.question: Evaluate the impact of marketisation on educational inequality.

points.text: Marketisation: schools compete like businesses (league tables, Ofsted, open enrollment). Positive: drives up standards, gives parents choice. questions.question: Assess whether comprehensive education has reduced inequality.

points.text: Comprehensives reduced the 11+ stigma and created more social mixing. However: streaming within comprehensives reproduced the tripartite divide (Ball: working-class in lower streams); middle-class parents still find ways to gain advantage (house buying, tutoring); the residual grammar schools in some areas maintain selection. Genuine equality requires addressing structural inequality outside as well as inside schools.
